intro: A solo guitarist with a mysterious, otherworldly voice.
story: Jessica Pratt played Pickathon in 2013 and returned in 2015, the year of On Your Own Love Again, her first for Drag City. She had recorded her 2012 self-titled debut at home, with songs reaching back to 2007, and made the follow-up the same way over about two years in Los Angeles and San Francisco. Quiet Signs followed on Mexican Summer in 2019, and Here in the Pitch in 2024 drew praise across the year-end lists. In 2025 she played festival and theater dates in Europe and California.
artist_reel_line: Here in the Pitch, in 2024, drew praise on year-end lists; Europe and California in 2025.

story: Tune-Yards is Merrill Garbus, whose looping vocals and polyrhythmic percussion stood out at Pickathon in 2015. Her w h o k i l l was voted best of 2011 in the Village Voice critics' poll, and Nikki Nack, on 4AD in 2014, reached No. 8 on Billboard's Top Rock Albums. She has played with bassist Nate Brenner since 2009. Better Dreaming came in 2025, followed by the EP Tell the Future With Your Body.
artist_reel_line: Better Dreaming, in 2025, was followed by the EP Tell the Future With Your Body.

intro: A songwriter stepping into his own.
story: Kevin Morby, a former Woods bassist and a founder of The Babies, was stepping into his own as a solo songwriter when he played Pickathon in 2015, two years after his debut Harlem River. He came back in 2016, the year of Singing Saw, his first for Dead Oceans, produced by Sam Cohen in Woodstock. City Music followed in 2017, Oh My God in 2019 and Sundowner in 2020. Little Wide Open, produced by Aaron Dessner, came in 2026, with a world tour.
artist_reel_line: Little Wide Open, produced by Aaron Dessner, came in 2026, with a world tour.

intro: A Brooklyn dream-pop band on the rise.
story: DIIV, a Brooklyn group led by Zachary Cole Smith, had Oshin on Captured Tracks in 2012 behind them when they played Pickathon in 2015. Is the Is Are, a 17-song double album, followed in 2016 and Deceiver in 2019, then Frog in Boiling Water in 2024. ZIRP!, produced by A. G. Cook, came out on Fantasy in 2026, and they toured North America with Interpol.
artist_reel_line: ZIRP!, produced by A. G. Cook, came in 2026, and a tour with Interpol.

intro: A cosmic spiritual-jazz saxophonist, just reaching beyond jazz.
story: Kamasi Washington arrived at Pickathon in 2015, the year The Epic came out on Brainfeeder: three CDs and 172 minutes, with a 32-piece orchestra and a 20-person choir. The Los Angeles saxophonist had played on recent records by Kendrick Lamar and Flying Lotus. Harmony of Difference followed in 2017 and Heaven and Earth in 2018. He became a festival regular and a film composer, with a 2020 Emmy nomination for the score to Becoming, and in fall 2026 he toured North America.
artist_reel_line: He scored Becoming, earned an Emmy nomination, and toured North America in fall 2026.
